findings.source_passage: Oh, trebly hooped and welded hip of power! Oh, high aspiring, rainbowed jet!—that one strivest, this one jettest all in vain!
findings.source_locator: final speech paragraph, third block of Ahab's monologue
findings.why_it_matters: The exclamation 'Oh, trebly hooped and welded hip of power!' is a distinctive, critically-noted piece of Melville's rhetoric linking back to the hoop/welding motifs of the novel; its complete omission in the draft (which jumps straight to 'Oh, high aspiring, rainbowed jet!') removes a textually distinctive and interpretively loaded phrase.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Oh, trebly hooped and welded hip of power!' verbatim before 'Oh, high aspiring, rainbowed jet!' in the third speech block.

findings.source_passage: Then hail, for ever hail, O sea, in whose eternal tossings the wild fowl finds his only rest. Born of earth, yet suckled by the sea; though hill and valley mothered me, ye billows are my foster-brothers!
findings.why_it_matters: The draft uses an ellipsis ('Then hail, for ever hail, O sea … ye billows are my foster-brothers!') that erases the entire middle of this celebrated closing apostrophe, including the 'wild fowl finds his only rest' image and the 'Born of earth, yet suckled by the sea; though hill and valley mothered me' lines—all of which are critically and rhetorically significant as the emotional culmination of the chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence: 'Then hail, for ever hail, O sea, in whose eternal tossings the wild fowl finds his only rest. Born of earth, yet suckled by the sea; though hill and valley mothered me, ye billows are my foster-brothers!' Do not use an ellipsis here.

findings.source_passage: Oh that these too-favouring eyes should see these too-favouring sights. Look! here, far water-locked … where to traditions no rocks furnish tablets
findings.why_it_matters: 'Oh that these too-favouring eyes should see these too-favouring sights' and 'where to traditions no rocks furnish tablets' are distinctive rhetorical formulations; the draft's ellipsis between 'baronial vassal of the sun!' and 'Look!' silently drops both, flattening the interpretive content about unmarked oceanic vastness.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Oh that these too-favouring eyes should see these too-favouring sights' and 'where to traditions no rocks furnish tablets' within the first speech block rather than using a bare ellipsis.

findings.source_passage: Yet dost thou, darker half, rock me with a prouder, if a darker faith.
findings.source_locator: third speech block, after 'all-quickening sun, that only calls forth life, but gives it not again'
findings.why_it_matters: This line is one of the key statements of Ahab's ambivalent attraction to the dark principle of nature and is interpretively central to readings of his fatalism; its omission from the draft leaves a gap in Ahab's theological argument.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Yet dost thou, darker half, rock me with a prouder, if a darker faith.' before 'All thy unnamable imminglings' in the third speech block.

findings.source_passage: Soothed again, but only soothed to deeper gloom, Ahab, who had sterned off from the whale, sat intently watching his final wanings from the now tranquil boat.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'his final wanings from the now tranquil boat' and the doubled 'Soothed again, but only soothed' rhythm are voice-establishing; the draft reduces this to 'But only soothed to deeper gloom, Ahab sterned off to watch,' stripping the watching/waning image and the syntactic doubling.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'sat intently watching his final wanings from the now tranquil boat' and the full 'Soothed again, but only soothed to deeper gloom' formulation.

summary: The draft drops two critically-significant verbatim passages (the 'trebly hooped' exclamation and the full final apostrophe to the sea) and silently omits several interpretively-loaded lines through unjustified ellipsis, constituting multiple high- and medium-severity signature losses.
